steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Expressive skills enable a dancer to communicate meaning, mood and intention to the audience

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Projection is the ability to reach out to the audience with energy and presence, making the performance compelling to watch

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Focus is the direction of the dancer's gaze and attention, guiding the audience's eye and expressing intention

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Musicality is the dancer's response to the music, showing awareness of rhythm, tempo, accents and phrasing through movement

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What is projection in dance and why does it matter? | Q: How can focus be used to show a dancer's relationship with a partner? | Q: Explain the difference between being on the beat and showing musicality.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Projection is the ability to extend energy and presence outward to engage the audience. It matters because it makes the performance compelling and ensures the audience connects with the dance. | A dancer can direct their gaze at a partner to show connection, look away to show distance, or use shared focus to demonstrate unity in the relationship. | Being on the beat means timing movements to the pulse; musicality goes further by responding to accents, dynamics, tempo changes and the emotional character of the music.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always link expressive skills back to the choreographic intention — do not describe them in isolation When writing about projection, mention both physical energy (extending through the body) and mental focus (engaging with the audience) Musicality questions often require specific references to how the dancer responds to rhythm, accents or dynamics Use the analogy of speech for phrasing — movements are grouped like sentences with pauses, emphasis and flow In 6-mark answers, cover at least two expressive skills and explain how each helps communicate meaning
